mentions.context_before: stochastic or genetic algorithms to randomly generate queries to test relational database systems [ 1,4]. In RAGS [ 4], queries are automatically generated and evaluated by multiple database systems. If the results are inconsistent, a bug has been found. While this method can be effective, it requires that the tested features be compatible with all tested query engines, and thus limited to only engine-specific SQL features that can be tested. MutaSQL generalizes this testing approach by comparing query results within the same database system so that the testing result can be directly verified.

analysis.summary: This short paper tests query execution engines by mutating queries in ways that preserve or predictably change their results, focusing on structural mutations such as inserting and removing subqueries. Published in 2020, it is contemporaneous with the first SQLancer oracles.
analysis.narrative: PQS is discussed in related work as the closest neighbour: the paper notes it also uses equivalence mutation, arranging for the mutated query to contain a specific row from the original output. The distinction drawn is one of level -- this work mutates query structure, while PQS mutates at the predicate level.
